key_insight: Online system identification coupled with nonlinear pseudo-spectral potential flow enables deterministic forecasts of coupled surge, heave, and pitch up to around eight wavelengths ahead.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support ship motion forecasting using onboard measurements while adapting to changing sea states without a complete pre-calibrated hydrodynamic model.
method: Identify three coupled motion equations from short free-running motion histories using constrained ridge regression.
Use a nonlinear pseudo-spectral potential-flow solver to forecast incident waves at the body's location.
Couple wave and motion models in a receding horizon, re-identifying coefficients online.
evidence_signal: Demonstration used validated CFD data for a freely floating two-dimensional rectangular box, showing accurate forecasts up to around eight wavelengths ahead and robustness to changing sea states.
watch_item: Performance on full-scale, three-dimensional ships with noisy onboard measurements remains to be established.
paper_title: Online Seakeeping Forecast Coupling System Identification With Nonlinear Pseudo Spectral Potential-Flow
